definition: In applied mathematics, multimodal optimization deals with optimization tasks that involve finding all or most of the multiple (at least locally optimal) solutions of a problem, as opposed to a single best solution.
details: Evolutionary multimodal optimization is a branch of evolutionary computation, which is closely related to machine learning. Wong provides a short survey, wherein the chapter of Shir and the book of Preuss cover the topic in more detail.

explainer.lead: Evolutionary multimodal optimization uses evolutionary search to find all or most of a problem's locally optimal solutions, not just one best answer. It matters when several good solutions are worth knowing about and choosing among.

tiers.eli5: Imagine exploring a landscape with several mountain peaks instead of only looking for the tallest one. You want a map showing all or most of the peaks, because each peak is a good answer in its own area. Evolutionary multimodal optimization searches for that collection of good answers.
tiers.practitioner: Use this approach when the required output is a set of locally optimal candidates rather than a single optimum. A common pitfall is stopping once the best candidate is found, which misses the multimodal goal; success instead depends on recovering all or most of the local optima.
tiers.paperLevel: For an objective f, the goal is to return a set S containing all or most locally optimal solutions x, rather than only one element of arg max f(x). Wong provides a short survey, while the chapter of Shir and the book of Preuss treat the topic in more detail.

explainer.example: Suppose a problem has three parameter settings, A, B, and C, each better than the nearby settings around it. A single-best-solution search might return only A, while evolutionary multimodal optimization seeks the set {A, B, C}, even if A has the highest overall objective value.

usedIn.name: Evolutionary computation
usedIn.detail: Provides the broader field of which evolutionary multimodal optimization is a branch.

usedIn.name: Machine learning
usedIn.detail: A closely related field, rather than the field that exclusively contains the topic.

explainer.intuition: A single best solution can hide other solutions that are optimal within their own regions. Multimodal optimization aims to uncover that wider set of answers.
howItWorks: Define an optimization problem that may have several locally optimal solutions.
Search with an evolutionary approach instead of pursuing only one final answer.
Identify solutions that are locally optimal in different parts of the problem.
Return all or most of those solutions as a set.
explainer.whyItMatters: It reveals multiple good answers when restricting the result to one optimum would discard useful solutions. This changes the goal from winning a single comparison to covering the problem's local optima.
misconceptions: It does not mean finding only the single globally best solution.
It is not itself a machine-learning model; it is a branch of evolutionary computation closely related to machine learning.
